reforms.description: The Bank of Japan introduced the Growth-Supporting Funding Facility in June 2010, providing long-term low-cost funding to financial institutions to encourage lending to firms in growth industries such as health and environment sectors. The scheme was expanded from 3 trillion yen to 5.5 trillion yen by March 2012.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directs credit to growth sectors (health and environment) to stimulate innovation and productive investment, though risks include postponing needed restructuring and resource misallocation through sectoral targeting.
reforms.status_evidence: The scheme was introduced in June 2010 and expanded in June 2011 and March 2012, with nearly 3.5 trillion yen disbursed.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant targeted credit facility supporting innovation in designated growth sectors, with substantial funding (5.5 trillion yen by 2012) and multi-year implementation, though narrower in scope than economy-wide R&D policy reform.
reforms.source_quote: The BoJ introduced the Growth-Supporting Funding Facility in June 2010 to directly encourage banks to lend to firms by providing long-term funding at low costs. The scheme was aimed at firms in growth industries, such as the health and environment sectors.

reforms.description: In October 2012, the Bank of Japan announced plans to establish a new fund-providing measure to stimulate bank lending without setting an upper limit to the total amount of funds supplied, later formalized as the Stimulating Bank Lending Facility in 2012 for implementation beginning June 2013.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Provides unlimited long-term funding at low cost to financial institutions to remove financing constraints on credit expansion, potentially supporting innovation and productive investment, though effectiveness depends on whether financing costs are the binding constraint.
reforms.status_evidence: The BoJ announced the facility in October 2012 and it began operation in June 2013, providing unlimited long-term funds at 0.1% to financial institutions.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant monetary policy instrument providing unlimited credit at near-zero rates to support lending, with economy-wide scope but narrower innovation focus than direct R&D funding reforms.
reforms.source_quote: In 2012, the BoJ announced the introduction of the Stimulating Bank Lending Facility to provide unlimited long-term funds at 0.1% to financial institutions, beginning in June 2013.

reforms.description: Japan announced a fiscal package in January 2013 that includes 3.1 trillion yen (2.2% of GDP) in measures to promote industrial competitiveness and innovation, alongside reconstruction and social spending.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Direct public investment in industrial competitiveness and innovation is intended to enhance productivity and technological capacity, supporting long-term growth potential.
reforms.status_evidence: In January 2013, the new government announced a 10.3 trillion yen fiscal package that includes measures to promote industrial competitiveness and innovation (3.1 trillion yen).
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant fiscal allocation to innovation and industrial competitiveness within a broader stimulus package, though the text does not specify the detailed mechanisms or sectoral focus of these measures.
reforms.source_quote: In January 2013, the new government announced a 10.3 trillion yen (2.2% of GDP) fiscal package that includes additional funds for the reconstruction of the Tohoku region and disaster prevention (3.8 trillion yen), social spending and regional revitalisation (3.1 trillion yen) and measures to promote industrial competitiveness and innovation (3.1 trillion yen).

reforms.description: The text recommends enhancing the role of the tertiary sector in innovation through greater cooperation between universities and the business sector, including enhanced labour mobility of researchers.
reforms.package_name: Education System Upgrade and Labour Participation Strategy
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhanced university-industry collaboration and researcher mobility strengthen knowledge transfer and applied research capacity, improving innovation outcomes and firm productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The text presents this as a recommendation in Box 3 summary of recommendations to boost labour participation and improve the education system.
reforms.importance_rationale: A meaningful policy recommendation to strengthen university-industry linkages and researcher mobility, which are important mechanisms for knowledge transfer and innovation, though presented as a recommendation rather than an implemented reform.
reforms.source_quote: Enhance the role of the tertiary sector in innovation, in part through greater co-operation between universities and the business sector, including enhanced labour mobility of researchers.

reforms.description: Japan established a government fund of 45 billion yen in FY2012 to support cooperation between university research and industry, strengthening knowledge transfer and collaborative innovation.
reforms.package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Direct support for university-industry collaboration accelerates knowledge transfer and commercialisation, enhancing firm-level innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The government is supporting university-industry cooperation through a fund of 45 billion yen in FY2012.
reforms.importance_rationale: A dedicated fund for university-industry cooperation represents a significant policy instrument for knowledge transfer and applied research, with meaningful economic relevance for innovation ecosystems.
reforms.source_quote: The government is supporting such co-operation through a fund of 45 billion yen in FY2012.

reforms.description: Japan's 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims to further allocate research funds on a competitive basis, shifting towards merit-based distribution of public research funding to universities.
reforms.package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Competitive allocation of research funds incentivises research excellence and efficiency, directing resources toward higher-impact research and improving allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at further allocating research funds on a competitive basis.
reforms.importance_rationale: A shift toward competitive allocation of research funding represents a significant governance reform affecting the distribution of public R&D resources, with implications for research quality and efficiency.
reforms.source_quote: Boost the share of public research funds for universities that is allocated competitively. The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at further allocating research funds on a competitive basis.

reforms.description: Japan's 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform promotes industry-academia cooperation to respond to labour market demands, including implementation of graduate school programmes conducted cooperatively with the business sector.
reforms.package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Cooperative graduate programmes build human capital aligned with industry needs and strengthen knowledge transfer, enhancing both research capacity and labour market outcomes.
reforms.status_evidence: The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at promoting industry-academia co-operation to respond to labour market demands, in part by implementing graduate school programmes co-operatively with the business sector.
reforms.importance_rationale: A structured approach to graduate-level industry-academia cooperation addresses both human capital development and knowledge transfer, with meaningful implications for applied research and firm innovation.
reforms.source_quote: The 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aims at promoting industry-academia co-operation to respond to labour market demands, in part by implementing graduate school programmes co-operatively with the business sector.

reforms.description: Japan increased public investment in programmes to create leading universities, raising funding from 12 billion yen in FY2011 to 21 billion yen in FY2012, with the 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform aiming to further allocate research funds on a competitive basis.
reforms.package_name: 2012 Action Plan for Higher Education Reform
reforms.component_name: Increased public investment in leading universities
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public R&D funding to universities enhances research capacity and human capital development, supporting long-term productivity growth and innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: Public investment in programmes to create leading universities increased from 12 billion yen in FY2011 to 21 billion yen in FY2012.
reforms.importance_rationale: A significant increase in university research funding (75% increase year-on-year) with explicit commitment to competitive allocation, supporting research excellence and institutional capacity-building.
reforms.source_quote: Public investment in programmes to create leading universities increased from 12 billion yen in FY2011 to 21 billion yen in FY2012. The 2012 'Action Plan for Higher Education Reform' aims at further allocating research funds on a competitive basis.
